text.p: The International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers filed a libel suit against Walt Disney Co seeking $200 million in damages for injuries to its reputation in the film "Ransom."
The suit, filed in Maryland Circuit Court in Prince Georges County, also named Richard Price and Alexander Ignon, the script's co-writers, as defendants.
The Machinists Union seeks $50 million in compensatory damages and three times that amount, or $150 million, in punitive damages.

John Walsh, attorney for the machinists, said the Machinists were unfairly portrayed as corrupt in the film, which stars Mel Gibson as the wealthy owner of an airline, whose son is kidnapped and held for a $2 million ransom.

"A key role in the movie's plot is that of a person clearly described as a corrupt 'Machinists Union' official, a description which is accompanied by references to 'Machinists Union indictments'", said Walsh.
Since the movie's November 2 release, he said there have been hundreds of inquiries and expressions of concern from members and the general public about these references.
Walsh said requests for Disney to modify and delete references to the Machinists Union have been rejected by Disney.
The references to the union have already resulted in damaging allegations about the Machinists Union in at least two major organizing campaigns since "Ransom" was released, Walsh said.
